2607.17770.title: Measuring Monosemanticity in Sparse Autoencoders via Latent Activation Coherence
2607.17770.paper_summary: Within Explainable Artificial Intelligence, mechanistic interpretability uses Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) to extract more interpretable features from neural representations. However, assessing their monosemanticity, and thus explanation quality, remains challenging. Existing metrics require external concept labels or depend on pretrained embedding models, making them sensitive to encoder's geometry. We introduce the Tversky Monosemanticity Score (TMS), a label-free metric that operationalizes monosemanticity as activation-set coherence of binarized SAE latents, and does not require external embedding encoders. We evaluate TMS on SAEs trained on features from pretrained vision and vision-language models (DINOv3, CLIP, BLIP2), two common SAE regimes (TopK, BatchTopK), multiple sparsity levels, and expansion factors. Our results show that TMS is less affected by encoder anisotropy than its embedding-based alternative, while remaining aligned with established monosemanticity indicators. TMS also reveals distinct SAE training dynamics across base models. Moreover, under encoder anisotropy, TMS provides a stronger indication of probe-based concept deletion effectiveness, while being competitive otherwise.
2607.17770.paper_summary_zh: 在可解釋的人工智慧中，機械解釋性使用稀疏自編碼器（SAEs）從神經表示中提取更具可解釋性的特徵。<lb/>然而，評估它們的單義性，因此解釋質量，仍然具有挑戰性。<lb/>現有的指標需要外部概念標籤或依賴於預訓練的嵌入模型，使其對編碼器的幾何形狀敏感。<lb/>我們引入了Tversky單義性分數（TMS），這是一種無標籤的指標，將單義性操作化為二元化SAE潛在變量的激活集一致性，並且不需要外部嵌入編碼器。<lb/>我們在基於預訓練視覺和視覺-語言模型（DINOv3、CLIP、BLIP2）的特徵上訓練的SAEs上評估TMS，兩種常見的SAE模式（TopK、BatchTopK）、多個稀疏性水平和擴展因子。<lb/>我們的結果顯示，TMS受到編碼器各向異性影響的程度低於其基於嵌入的替代品，同時與已建立的單義性指標保持一致。<lb/>TMS還揭示了基礎模型之間的不同SAE訓練動態。<lb/>此外，在編碼器各向異性的情況下，TMS提供了更強的探針基於概念刪除有效性的指示，而在其他情況下也具有競爭力。
